items.text: Why Copilot Can't Answer Questions About Your ERP
Three issues stop most Microsoft-centric organizations from moving AI agents beyond a pilot.
Copilot Isn't Grounded In Your Business Systems
Copilot works across Microsoft 365 files, mail, and chat. Records in Dynamics 365, SAP, or a custom application sit outside that boundary, so it has no way to retrieve them.
Point Solutions Don't Scale
Individual teams build their own plugins, scripts, and exports. The result is duplicated work and no central record of which agent can access which system.
Existing Access Controls Don't Cover Agents
Controls built for users and services don't fit an agent that writes to finance data. Security teams won't approve it without a clear permission and audit model.

items.text: MCP Servers for the Systems You Run
We build connectors for the systems that hold your operational data, including the ones generic MCP tooling doesn't support.
Microsoft Dynamics 365

Agents work directly against Business Central and Finance and Operations, including custom fields, to retrieve orders and invoices, create sales orders, query inventory, and route approvals against posting rules.
SAP
We connect through the interfaces SAP actually exposes — BAPIs, IDocs, and OData from S/4HANA and ECC — to call material and order operations and enforce SAP authorization objects on every call.
Oracle NetSuite
For organizations running NetSuite alongside Microsoft systems, agents query transactions through SuiteQL, create and amend sales orders, and reconcile records against Dynamics 365.
Custom Applications
We build an MCP server directly over internal apps, data warehouses, and third-party APIs, including read-only database access where no API exists, rather than waiting for a replacement project.
Legacy & On-Premises Systems
Outbound-only connectivity and Azure Private Link bring cloud agents to Dynamics AX, GP, NAV, and SAP ECC behind the firewall, with no inbound rules and no VPN.

items.text: Deployed in Your Azure Tenant
The MCP layer runs on Azure services your platform team already uses and governs.
Microsoft Entra ID
Agents authenticate and authorize against your existing directory, with role-based access control and single sign-on.
Azure Kubernetes Service
MCP servers run containerized in your subscription, scaling with demand and patched on your schedule.
Azure Key Vault
System credentials and secrets stay inside your boundary, with rotation under your existing policy.
Azure Monitor
Every tool call is traced with identity, arguments, and outcome, feeding your existing dashboards and alerts.

items.text: Security and Audit Controls
Your security team will ask what an agent can do, who authorized it, and what it did — with controls mapped to ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and Microsoft Solutions Partner status.
Every Tool Is Explicitly Registered
Every action an agent can call is declared and reviewed before release, so there is a definitive list of what is permitted.
Authorization on Every Call
Permission is checked per request against Microsoft Entra ID, scoped to the task. Write operations can require human approval.
Full Audit Trail
Identity, arguments, decision, and outcome are logged for every call, so any agent action can be traced after the fact.

items.text: Real Results, Real Impact
Frequently Asked Questions
Answers to the questions we hear most about enterprise MCP on Azure.

Copilot is grounded in Microsoft 365 content such as files, mail, and chat. Records in Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, or a custom application sit outside that boundary. An MCP server exposes those records as callable actions, so Copilot can retrieve a purchase order or post an update to the system.

We deliver the MCP servers: tool definitions, connector code for each system, identity and authorization through Microsoft Entra ID, deployment into your Azure subscription, and logging and tracing for agent activity. Engagements start with an assessment and can continue into build and managed operations.

Yes. The MCP servers are deployed into your Azure subscription and the source code is yours, with documentation and knowledge transfer at handover. You can run it with your own platform team or retain us for managed operations.

Inside your tenant. MCP servers are containerized on Azure Kubernetes Service or Azure Container Apps within your subscription, secrets are held in Azure Key Vault, and traffic to systems can be kept off the public internet using Azure Private Link. Your data does not transit a vendor cloud.

Microsoft Dynamics 365, including Business Central and Finance and Operations, along with SAP, Oracle NetSuite, and older estates on Microsoft Dynamics AX, GP, and NAV. We also build MCP servers for custom line of business applications, data warehouses, and third-party APIs where no connector exists.

Agent permissions are modeled the same way user permissions are. Each tool is registered explicitly, authorization is enforced through Microsoft Entra ID on every call, write operations can require human approval, and each request is logged in Azure Monitor with the identity, arguments, and result.

The assessment runs two weeks and delivers a working prototype against one system. A first production MCP server typically follows in six to eight weeks, depending on system complexity and your security review cycle. Additional systems are faster because the platform work is already complete.

Yes. MCP is an open standard, so the servers we build are callable by Copilot, Copilot Studio agents, Claude, ChatGPT, and any custom orchestration. You are not committed to one assistant, and you can add another without rebuilding the integration.
